To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
opiate receptors of MSA participate in the regulation of fluid and electrolyte homeostasis, blood pressure and drinking.
the opiate activation in the medial septal region suppresses the drinking and pressor responses induced by choline activation.
the cholinergic stimulation induces natriuresis and kaliuresis, increases blood pressure and drinking and reduces urine output.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the participation and interaction among cholinergic, opiate and adrenergic receptors in the regulation of cardiovascular and fluid-electrolyte homeostasis.
the participation of the septal cholinergic neurons on the cardiovascular, fluid and sodium excretion regulation and the possible interaction between cholinergie and opiate receptors in the MSA.

the participation and interaction of opiate and cholinergic receptors of the medial preoptic area (MPOA) in the modulation of cardiovascular, fluid and sodium excretion and drinking responses in rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cholinergic and the opiate systems of the medial septum have an inhibitory influence on the cardiovascular, water and electrolyte balance regulation.
opiate activation in the MSA suppresses the drinking and pressor responses induced by choline activation of the MSA.
cholinergic stimulation induces an increase in the secretion of ADH and renin, which in turn, induce a natriuretic, diuretic and hypertensive response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cholinergic and opioid receptors are involved in the regulation of cardiovascular, fluid and salt balance in the MSA of the rat.
cholinergic stimulation in the MSA induces a natriuresis, diuresis and pressor response.
the cholinergic and opioidergic systems interact in the regulation of fluid, electrolyte and cardiovascular homeostasis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cholinergic system of the MSA is involved in the regulation of water, electrolyte and blood pressure balance, and that the opiate system is a physiological modulator of this system.
the cholinergic stimulation is a powerful regulator of the renal function, and it is modulated by opiate receptors of medial septal area.
cholinergic stimulation increases the activity of the sympathetic nervous system and the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system and the opiate activation suppresses the activity of both systems.
